transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-21 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (LumaSearch - Head of Search), Tom Becker (LumaSearch - Eng Mgr), Elena Park (LumaSearch - Data Scientist)
Links shared: Redwood hosted demo deck (link), benchmark spreadsheet (link), security overview (SOC2) (link)

Summary: quick hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings + reranking for LumaSearch's product search relevance use case. Showed embeddings endpoint, vector similarity, and Redwood rerank endpoint that uses embeddings + fast cross-encoder style re-ranking. Discussed latency/cost tradeoffs and pilot steps.

Topics: Hosted embeddings API, rerank endpoint, hybrid search (BM25 + embeddings), API keys & trial provisioning, perf benchmarks, evaluation metrics (MRR, NDCG), security/SOC2 docs.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
[00:05] Priya: yes, sounds good, thanks Maya.
[00:09] Maya: cool, i'm Maya from Redwood, i'll run the demo and Carlos will jump into the deeper technical bits. quick round — can you remind us your main goals for relevance?
[00:20] Priya: sure, our goal is to improve product search precision for tail queries while keeping latency under 150 ms median for web traffic. we currently use a hybrid approach with Elastic + a model embedding service, but results are noisy for long, complex queries.
[00:36] Tom: also cost — our infra spend on embedding storage and cross-encoder re-ranks is rising, so we want predictable per-query costs.
[00:44] Carlos: makes sense. you'll be familiar with the hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs — hosted gives fastest path to trial, we can provision a sandbox and throttle usage.
[00:53] Priya: yeah hosted trial would be ideal for an initial benchmark.
[00:58] Maya: perfect. i'll share my screen and walk through the hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints, show a notebook, and then Carlos will show perf and routing.
[01:10] Maya: (screen) this is our hosted api quickstart doc — you can call /v1/embeddings with the model param, get back a vector, we support dimension 1536 and 1024 variants depending on model. note: we also provide batched embeddings to reduce tokenization overhead.
[01:30] Elena: quick q — do you support incremental updates to vectors or is it full reindex?
[01:35] Carlos: currently we expect you to push vectors to your vector DB (we're DB-agnostic). Redwood's platform caches prefixes and can cache hot vectors at serving time to reduce fetches, but for index updates you'll push deltas to your vector store.
[01:48] Priya: got it. do you have recommended vector DB partners?
[01:51] Maya: we often see customers use Pinecone, Milvus, and managed vectors from cloud providers. for our hosted demo we'll show a simple in-memory example in the notebook.
[02:01] Maya: moving on, here's the rerank endpoint — pattern is: fetch top-K candidates from vector db (or BM25), then call /v1/rerank with query + candidates; rerank returns a scored ordering. this preserves throughput because the rerank stage runs on a compact cross-attention model optimized for latency.
[02:24] Tom: what's the expected latency for rerank on ~10 candidates?
[02:28] Carlos: in hosted mode, using our optimized kernels, you can expect ~20–40 ms per rerank call for 10 candidates on standard plans; if you push to dedicated you can get even lower tail latency. those numbers are model-dependent, but we've tuned the default rerank model for low-latency cross-encoder scoring.
[02:44] Priya: and cost?
[02:46] Maya: cost is per-request for rerank plus embedding generation cost amortized across candidates. for the trial we'll send a pricing estimate based on your expected qps — i'll include that in the follow-up.
[02:58] [03:05] Carlos: demo time — opening the notebook, i'll send a sample query "waterproof hiking backpack under $150" and show vector search + rerank.
[03:15] Carlos: (typing) first step is embeddings call, here's the curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"model":"rwd-sim-1536","input":["...queries..."]}' you get vectors back in JSON, we show cosine-normalized results.
[03:36] Elena: transcription glitch - you said rwd-sim, is that your labeled sim model?
[03:39] Carlos: yeah rwd-sim-1536 is our similarity model name in hosted catalog, sorry the doc abbreviates it. sometimes the catalog shows rwd-sim or r-sim in the SDK, but the API accepts model alias or id.
[03:52] Carlos: next we run a top-k candidate fetch from an in-memory index, then call /v1/rerank with the query and the 10 hits payload. here's the request — it returns scores and a rationale field with highlights (if you enable structured output).
[04:08] Priya: highlight field sounds useful for UI explainability, is that on by default?
[04:12] Maya: it's optional — enabling structured output increases payload size slightly but can help you debug ranking issues; we can include that in the trial config.
[04:20] Tom: do you do any caching to avoid reranking for repeated queries?
[04:23] Carlos: yes, Redwood has prefix/KV caching and result-level caching. for high-frequency queries we can serve cached reranks which reduces cost significantly. caching is workload-aware and respects freshness rules.
[04:36] [04:40] Maya: quick aside on hybrid search — many customers combine BM25 for recall and embeddings for semantic re-ordering. that keeps recall high and uses rerank to push relevant items up.
[04:50] Priya: our current problem is long tail — sometimes BM25 finds items but ordering is off. so rerank should help.
[04:56] Carlos: exactly. for long complex multi-attribute queries rerank gives contextual scoring that BM25 can't capture.
[05:02] Maya: now i'll show the console briefly — (screen) here's per-route latency, cost per token, and token breakdown. you can set SLO routes to prefer cheaper sim model for non-critical traffic and fallback to cross-encoder rerank for critical flows.
[05:21] Elena: can we do canary rollouts of rerank models?
[05:24] Carlos: yes, console supports canary and A/B rollouts by route. you can send 5% of traffic to a candidate rerank model and compare NDCG on heldout test queries in our eval pipeline.
[05:36] Priya: do you store logs for evaluation? data residency concerns?
[05:40] Maya: we have configurable retention and data residency options; hosted standard retention is 30 days, enterprise options for longer retention in specific regions plus SOC2 controls. i'll attach the SOC2 and data residency doc.
[05:51] Tom: also curious about SSO and RBAC for the console.
[05:54] Maya: we support SAML SSO, SCIM, RBAC roles for routes and keys. enterprise private deployments can connect to your KMS for key control.
[06:02] [06:10] Carlos: back to performance — for the demo i ran a repeat of 1k queries offline, saw median embed latency ~12 ms for batch size 8, median rerank 28 ms for 10 candidates. those were run against hosted sandbox GPUs and our optimized kernel paths.
[06:28] Priya: nice. what's the expected throughput? we might spike to 500 qps for peak events.
[06:33] Carlos: in hosted setup throughput depends on batch tuning and autoscaling; Redwood AGENT pools can autoscale pods, and we have dedicated capacity options for reserved throughput. for 500 qps you'll likely want a dedicated pool with autoscaling buffer, or use routing policy to spill to lower-cost models for non-critical queries.
[06:51] Priya: what's the integration effort? we have a React front end and node-based backend.
[06:55] Maya: typical integration is a few days to wire embeddings into your vector DB ingestion pipeline and a week to add rerank calls in the service layer and run A/B tests. for the pilot we provide example node/ts SDK code and an end-to-end notebook.
[07:08] Tom: and will the pilot include billing? we want to see cost vs current setup.
[07:12] Maya: yes, we'll provide a pilot credit for the hosted sandbox and estimate costs; full pricing will be in the pilot agreement.
[07:20] [07:30] Elena: can Redwood's rerank support multi-lingual product queries? we operate in EN/ES/FR.
[07:35] Carlos: we have multi-lingual support in our embeddings models; rerank models can be fine-tuned or you can pick language-specific sim models. we'll surface model performance per language in the report.
[07:47] Priya: great. can you run a small comparison to our current Elastic + cross-encoder pipeline?
[07:51] Carlos: yes that's part of the benchmark plan — we compare MRR/NDCG and tail-latency. we'll need a sample of your query logs and relevance judgments or clicks to evaluate.
[08:02] Maya: (notes) next steps: we'll send pilot agreement, provision keys, request sample logs.
[08:07] Priya: timeline — we want a pilot in June, run for 2 weeks, then decide on dedicated in July. does that align?
[08:14] Maya: yes that works. we'll aim to have keys and benchmark template by 2026-05-24 so you can kick off week of 2026-06-08.
[08:24] Tom: security review — can you provide SOC2 + data processing addendum for legal?
[08:29] Maya: yes i'll attach SOC2 report and DPA in the follow-up.
[08:33] Priya: any limitations for product catalogs with many variants (sizes/colors)?
[08:37] Carlos: not really, rerank uses the candidate's attributes too if you include them in payload. we often pass product metadata and let the model use both text and structured features, and you can add business rules post-rerank for mandatory filters.
[08:50] [09:00] Maya: quick demo of structured output — here's a rerank response with scores and an explain snippet: {"candidate_scores": [...], "rationale":"matches on waterproof + size match"} (note: transcript paraphrased).
[09:14] Elena: small note — transcription seems to clobber some product names, but we get the idea.
[09:18] Maya: yeah auto-transcripts are imperfect.
[09:21] Carlos: performance knobs: batching, quantized models for lower cost but slightly higher latency, and serving policies. Redwood Optimize can run model/quant recommendations for your workload to hit cost targets while preserving MRR.
[09:37] Priya: is quantization safe for us? we care about ranking quality.
[09:40] Carlos: for similarity embedding models, int8/4 quantization often preserves cosine similarity well. for rerank cross-encoders we recommend evaluating; Optimize will surface expected regression and can holdout regression thresholds.
[09:55] Priya: good. can we try both quantized and full-precision in the pilot?
[09:58] Maya: yes that's a good A/B test — we'll include that in the plan.
[10:03] [10:12] Maya: ok final recap — action items and timeline: Maya send pricing/pilot, Carlos provision keys + notebook + benchmark template, Priya provide logs. pilot: week of 2026-06-08 for 2 weeks. security docs attached.
[10:30] Priya: sounds good, thanks all.
[10:33] Tom: thanks.
[10:36] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with docs and a calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff.
[10:42] End of recording.
